locators: pp.331–332, reverse reaction and HG/HMG equilibrium paragraphs; Figures3 and4
interpretation: The generic RHEA:18172 bidirectional identity is consistent with the reported reverse HG assay. The authors consider equilibrium among optical l-HG, pyruvate and glyoxylate while d-HG remains practically inert; the approximate HG equilibrium constant is 0.03±0.01 M (pH8,25°C), HMG about0.07±0.02 M. CHA does not reach equilibrium because oxaloacetate decarboxylation drains product. This does not establish in vivo equilibrium, equal enantiomer turnover, or R/S identity.
